relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition supports the IPv4 and IPv6 address families.

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; object stands in for 'auto-failover disabled'
relations.evidence: Auto-failover must be disabled prior to the changeover (and can be re-enabled _after_ the changeover).

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; object stands in for 'node-to-node encryption disabled'
relations.evidence: Node-to-node encryption must be disabled prior to the changeover (and can be re-enabled _after_ the changeover).

relations.subject: server:cluster-encryption-level
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; the level's own value gates whether the encryption feature can be turned off at all
relations.evidence: If node-to-node encryption needs to be disabled, ensure that the `clusterEncryptionLevel` for the cluster is set to `control`, rather than all — otherwise node-to-node encryption cannot be disabled.

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.evidence: `Cluster using ipv4only`: Every node in the cluster is using IPv4, and may _not_ use IPv6\. (This message is generated only by Couchbase Server Version 7.0.2 and later.)

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call standing in for the dual-stack networking capability each node must have, since the registry has no dedicated 'dual-stack networking' concept
relations.evidence: Each cluster-node must be operating in _dual stack_ mode, thereby supporting both IPv4 and IPv6 addressing.

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call standing in for 'nodes named by raw IP address', since the registry has no dedicated node-naming-scheme concept
relations.evidence: The address family can only be changed if each cluster-node is named with a fully qualified domain-name (such as `nodename.clustername.com`). Raw IP addresses _can_ be used to name cluster-nodes, but the cluster must be _created_ with them, and the address family cannot subsequently be changed.

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call, object stands in for 'every non-Data service', since the affected set is a whole class rather than one named service
relations.evidence: On each node, when the address-family change occurs, all Couchbase Services hosted on that node _other than_ the Data Service are restarted.

relations.subject: server:cluster-address-family
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, the explicit negation partner to the cascadesTo relation immediately above
relations.evidence: On each node, when the address-family change occurs, all Couchbase Services hosted on that node _other than_ the Data Service are restarted.

notable_absence.finding: No role requirement is stated anywhere on this page for the ip-family CLI command sequence, unlike node-addition and modify-services, both of which name Full/Cluster Admin explicitly. This is a real, checkable gap rather than a deliberate omission: changing a whole cluster's address family is at least as consequential as adding a node, yet the docs are silent on who is authorized to do it.

cross_component_finding: This page provides the missing half of the precondition chain flagged in apply-node-to-node-encryption.json's cross_component_finding: an address-family changeover requires BOTH auto-failover and node-to-node encryption to be off first, and disabling node-to-node encryption itself requires clusterEncryptionLevel=control. Three distinct minted/reused mechanisms (server:cluster-address-family, server:auto-failover, tls:node-to-node-encryption, server:cluster-encryption-level) form a single stated dependency chain that no individual page states in full - each page only names its own immediate precondition.
